channel.title: Acme: Light News
channel.description: Positive, lighthearted and unusual current news.

item.title: Runaway 30-foot pumpkin rolls down a North Carolina road
item.description: A giant inflatable pumpkin broke loose from Phillips Farms in Cary and tumbled down a road, sending motorists into reverse. An Uber driver and other witnesses helped corral and deflate the 30-foot decoration. The farm returned it to Pumpkinfest and thanked the good Samaritans with free festival tickets.

item.title: Wife's advice turns familiar lottery numbers into $250,000
item.description: James Mosley of High Shoals, North Carolina, nearly abandoned the family-birthday numbers he had played for years, but his wife persuaded him to stick with them. The ticket matched four white balls and the Powerball; a 5X multiplier raised the prize to $250,000. He plans to put some of it toward remodeling their home.

item.title: Deputies stage a roadside rodeo for three loose animals
item.description: Bexar County deputies found two horses and a donkey wandering dangerously close to Interstate 35 and improvised an evening roundup. The sheriff's office said all three animals were safely reunited with their owner, who then took measures to keep them secured.

item.title: English grower raises record 2,856-pound pumpkin
item.description: Ian Paton of Hampshire grew Bagheera, a 2,856.8-pound pumpkin certified as the world's heaviest at a weigh-off in Wargrave. The 20-foot-around gourd outweighed the previous record by about 45 pounds and, at its thirstiest, needed roughly 130 gallons of water a day.

item.title: Giant fungus earns the name D-rex
item.description: Scientists have described Dianjunus rex, nicknamed D-rex, from the forests of Yunnan, China. Its fruiting body can reach 20 inches and five pounds, enormous by mushroom standards. Genetic work places the unusual species in a newly named genus and family whose lineage may stretch back about 65 million years.

item.title: Moviegoer raises $146,000 for longtime theater worker
item.description: After 21-year-old Brooklyn Green met Mary, who had worked at Tennessee movie theaters for more than 45 years, she posted a video and organized a fundraiser to help her retire. Viewers responded with $146,000, turning an ordinary trip to the movies into an extraordinary thank-you.

item.title: A softball game reunites long-lost sisters
item.description: Montana teen Samantha Rensvold knew she had a biological sister but had never met her. A teammate noticed that an opposing softball player looked remarkably like Samantha, and the hunch led her to 18-year-old Kyann Dean. The sisters even discovered they both play volleyball in the same position and wear the same number.

item.title: Berlin app tells residents when street trees are thirsty
item.description: An open-source map called Gieß den Kiez helps Berliners care for nearly 900,000 street trees. Residents can “adopt” a tree, see nearby public water taps and get watering guidance based on species, age, location and weather. The project turns routine walks into a neighborhood conservation effort.

item.title: A childhood lemonade stand grows into a $5 million charity
item.description: Payton Obert began selling lemonade at age 8 to repay the kindness she remembered from a hospital stay as a toddler. Her annual stand has grown into a multi-state charity effort that has delivered $5 million in gifts and necessities to children and families, including $170,000 raised in its 2026 edition.

item.title: East Texas family sells lakefront land for a future state park
item.description: The Pollard family sold 650 acres on Lake Palestine to the Texas Parks and Wildlife Foundation for $35 million so the land can become a state park. The property includes pine woods, wetlands, bluffs and a working pecan orchard, with room for camping, paddling, fishing and wildlife watching.

item.title: Aldabra's giant tortoise population reaches about 180,000
item.description: A five-year survey estimates nearly 183,000 adult and sub-adult giant tortoises now roam Aldabra Atoll in the Seychelles, up from fewer than 1,000 in the 19th century. Researchers call the rebound one of the Indian Ocean's great conservation successes while warning that drought and invasive animals remain threats.

item.title: Personalized walking change eases arthritic knee pain
item.description: In a year-long randomized trial, people with knee osteoarthritis who learned a personalized change in foot angle reported less pain and showed slower cartilage deterioration than a placebo group. Researchers used motion analysis to determine whether each participant should turn a foot slightly inward or outward.

item.title: Sloth bear named by Julia Roberts flourishes after rescue
item.description: Odum, a sloth bear rescued from forced street performances in India 17 years ago, is thriving at the Bannerghatta Bear Rescue Centre. Julia Roberts named him during a 2009 visit. Now 26, he spends his days foraging, climbing and enjoying the companionship of other rescued bears.

item.title: Pilot daughter shares cockpit with dad while mom works cabin
item.description: A surprise KLM assignment gave 22-year-old co-pilot Zoë de Bruijn a flight with her father as captain and her mother serving in the cabin. The family had long joked about someday working the same trip, turning an ordinary roster change into a full-circle aviation memory.

item.title: £300 salvage-yard statue may be lost work by Trevi Fountain sculptor
item.description: A marble model bought for £300 at a Wiltshire salvage yard has been identified as a likely work by Pietro Bracci, the sculptor behind the Trevi Fountain's central figure. Experts believe the papal bust was a presentation model for a lost monumental bronze and estimate it could fetch £6,600 to £13,300.
